examFormat.heading: Claude Certified Developer Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: The exam is proctored online. Here is the format:
examFormat.scenarioPercent: The practice scenarios describe an API or integration problem and ask which behavior or application change addresses it.
bestWayToPass: Build a small project: Create an app or command-line tool that calls the Claude API, then debug the complete request flow.
Practise tool use: Define schemas, handle tool requests, return results, and test errors across multiple turns.
Create an evaluation: Run a set of inputs against a prompt, review outputs, and compare results after a change.
Use official documentation: Review Anthropic’s API, prompt, and tool-use guides for current behavior.

keyConcepts.h2: Claude Certified Developer: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: Messages API Requests
blocks.body: A Messages API request includes the model, token limit and conversation messages. Your application should handle the returned content and API errors.

blocks.heading: Prompts and Untrusted Input
blocks.body: Keep trusted instructions separate from user-provided content. Treat retrieved documents and user text as data, not as authority to change the application’s rules.

blocks.heading: SDKs and Credentials
blocks.body: Use the supported SDK or HTTP interface and keep API keys in protected configuration. Revoke exposed keys and review usage after a leak.

blocks.heading: Tools and Agents
blocks.body: Describe each tool’s purpose, parameters and result. The application executes tool calls and returns results; validate inputs and handle failures.

blocks.heading: Testing and Evaluation
blocks.body: Build evaluations from representative examples. Run them when prompts or model versions change, inspect regressions and deploy only when the results meet the product bar.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Claude Certified Developer Exam
scenarioTips.intro: Read the request, response or failure details, then identify what the application must handle.

blocks.heading: Handle API responses defensively
blocks.body: Plan for overloads, invalid requests and context limits; use bounded retries only for transient failures.

blocks.heading: Validate structured output
blocks.body: Describe the expected format and check the response in application code before using it.

blocks.heading: Use tools for external data
blocks.body: Keep database lookups and other actions in tools the application controls.

blocks.heading: Test before changing models
blocks.body: Run a representative evaluation set and review failures before deployment.

sampleQuestions.question: A support assistant must retrieve an order status from a database before answering. What should the application use?
options: Call a database lookup tool
A higher temperature so Claude can guess
A full database dump in the system prompt
A fine-tuned model with no retrieval path
sampleQuestions.explanation: A tool lets Claude request a database lookup; the application executes it and returns the result for Claude to use.
whyWrong: A higher temperature so Claude can guess does not fit because it addresses a different need than A database lookup tool with a schema Claude can call.
A full database dump in the system prompt does not fit because it addresses a different need than A database lookup tool with a schema Claude can call.
A fine-tuned model with no retrieval path does not fit because it addresses a different need than A database lookup tool with a schema Claude can call.

sampleQuestions.question: The Messages API returns HTTP 529. What response is appropriate?
options: Replace the API key immediately
Retry with exponential backoff
Rewrite the JSON request body
Disable authentication for the next call
sampleQuestions.explanation: A 529 indicates temporary API overload. Backoff and retry help avoid adding load during the incident.
whyWrong: Replace the API key immediately does not fit because it addresses a different need than Retry with exponential backoff after a delay.
Rewrite the JSON request body does not fit because it addresses a different need than Retry with exponential backoff after a delay.
Disable authentication for the next call does not fit because it addresses a different need than Retry with exponential backoff after a delay.

sampleQuestions.question: Why should user-supplied instructions not be placed directly in the system prompt?
options: System prompts have a 100-token maximum
It makes every request cost more than a user message
Untrusted text can inject conflicting instructions
Claude changes languages whenever a system prompt contains user text
sampleQuestions.explanation: User-provided text is untrusted. Keep it in the user message and design the application so it cannot override trusted instructions.
whyWrong: System prompts have a 100-token maximum does not fit because it addresses a different need than Untrusted text could act as prompt injection and conflict with intended behavior.
It makes every request cost more than a user message does not fit because it addresses a different need than Untrusted text could act as prompt injection and conflict with intended behavior.

Claude changes languages whenever a system prompt contains user text does not fit because it addresses a different need than Untrusted text could act as prompt injection and conflict with intended behavior.

sampleQuestions.question: An application needs JSON with summary, sentiment and confidence fields. Which approach is most reliable?
options: Ask for JSON once and trust every response
Set max tokens to the expected character count
Extract braces with a regular expression only
Specify a schema and validate output
sampleQuestions.explanation: A clear schema and defensive parsing reduce format errors; the application should still handle responses that do not match.
whyWrong: Ask for JSON once and trust every response does not fit because it addresses a different need than Specify the schema and validate or handle the returned data.
Set max tokens to the expected character count does not fit because it addresses a different need than Specify the schema and validate or handle the returned data.
Extract braces with a regular expression only does not fit because it addresses a different need than Specify the schema and validate or handle the returned data.

sampleQuestions.question: When is streaming a useful response mode?
options: Stream for interactive progressive output
For every request because it always costs less
Only when a response is exactly 100 tokens
Never, because streaming is unsupported
sampleQuestions.explanation: Streaming is useful when users benefit from seeing an interactive response arrive progressively.
whyWrong: For every request because it always costs less does not fit because it addresses a different need than For an interactive interface where showing text as it arrives improves perceived latency.
Only when a response is exactly 100 tokens does not fit because it addresses a different need than For an interactive interface where showing text as it arrives improves perceived latency.
Never, because streaming is unsupported does not fit because it addresses a different need than For an interactive interface where showing text as it arrives improves perceived latency.

sampleQuestions.question: A newer Claude model performs worse on a feature than the model it replaces. What should the team do?
options: Switch back permanently and stop evaluating updates
Run evals before deploying the model
Assume a newer model is always better
Wait for a vendor change without testing the application
sampleQuestions.explanation: Run the existing evals against the new model, investigate failed cases and deploy only after the application meets its quality bar.
whyWrong: Switch back permanently and stop evaluating updates does not fit because it addresses a different need than Run the evaluation suite, inspect regressions and deploy only when results meet the bar.
Assume a newer model is always better does not fit because it addresses a different need than Run the evaluation suite, inspect regressions and deploy only when results meet the bar.

Wait for a vendor change without testing the application does not fit because it addresses a different need than Run the evaluation suite, inspect regressions and deploy only when results meet the bar.

sampleQuestions.question: What should an application do when a conversation is approaching the model’s context limit?
options: Assume Claude will always summarize older messages
Continue sending the full history and ignore errors
Trim or summarize history before sending
Increase max_tokens to expand the context window
sampleQuestions.explanation: The application must manage conversation history before it exceeds the model’s context limit.
whyWrong: Assume Claude will always summarize older messages does not fit because it addresses a different need than Manage the history through trimming, summarization or splitting before sending.
Continue sending the full history and ignore errors does not fit because it addresses a different need than Manage the history through trimming, summarization or splitting before sending.
Increase max_tokens to expand the context window does not fit because it addresses a different need than Manage the history through trimming, summarization or splitting before sending.

sampleQuestions.question: A team needs to classify 10,000 support tickets without an interactive response. Which approach fits?
options: Send all tickets in one enormous prompt
Call the synchronous endpoint in a loop with no error handling
Have staff paste each ticket into a chat
Use the Batches API
sampleQuestions.explanation: The Batches API is designed for high-volume asynchronous work and is more suitable than one huge prompt or unguarded synchronous calls.
whyWrong: Send all tickets in one enormous prompt does not fit because it addresses a different need than Submit the requests through the Batches API and retrieve results later.
Call the synchronous endpoint in a loop with no error handling does not fit because it addresses a different need than Submit the requests through the Batches API and retrieve results later.
Have staff paste each ticket into a chat does not fit because it addresses a different need than Submit the requests through the Batches API and retrieve results later.

sampleQuestions.question: An API key was committed to a public repository. What is the immediate risk?
options: An exposed key permits billable API calls
The key expires automatically when GitHub sees it
GitHub blocks every request using the key
There is no risk if the repository is later deleted
sampleQuestions.explanation: A public key can be copied and used by others, creating unauthorized usage and charges. Revoke it and replace it.
whyWrong: The key expires automatically when GitHub sees it does not fit because it addresses a different need than Anyone who finds it may make billable API calls with the key.
GitHub blocks every request using the key does not fit because it addresses a different need than Anyone who finds it may make billable API calls with the key.
There is no risk if the repository is later deleted does not fit because it addresses a different need than Anyone who finds it may make billable API calls with the key.

sampleQuestions.question: What makes a tool description useful to Claude?
options: A one-word name with no details
Describe purpose, inputs and output
A programming language Claude can compile
An empty description so Claude can infer behavior
sampleQuestions.explanation: A clear description helps Claude decide when and how to call the tool and understand its inputs and outputs.
whyWrong: A one-word name with no details does not fit because it addresses a different need than A clear explanation of purpose, when to use it, parameters and returned data.
A programming language Claude can compile does not fit because it addresses a different need than A clear explanation of purpose, when to use it, parameters and returned data.
An empty description so Claude can infer behavior does not fit because it addresses a different need than A clear explanation of purpose, when to use it, parameters and returned data.

sampleQuestions.question: An app receives a tool-use request from Claude. What should it check before acting?
options: Execute the returned action because Claude chose the tool
Treat every returned argument as trusted input from the application
Validate the tool and arguments, then enforce application permissions
Run the action first and inspect its effects if anything looks wrong
sampleQuestions.explanation: Validate the requested tool and arguments, then enforce application authorization.
whyWrong: The model’s selection does not replace application-side validation or authorization.
Tool arguments are model output and must be checked before use.
Post-action inspection cannot prevent an unauthorized or harmful side effect.

sampleQuestions.question: A client gets an intermittent rate-limit response. What retry behavior is appropriate?
options: Retry a limited number of times with backoff and server guidance
Retry immediately in a tight loop until a request succeeds
Repeat requests without a limit and ignore retry instructions
Drop the request silently without recording or reporting the failure
sampleQuestions.explanation: Use bounded retries with backoff and respect any server retry guidance.
whyWrong: A tight loop can intensify the rate limit and burden the service.
Unbounded retries can create load and disregard server guidance.
Silently losing work makes failures hard to detect and recover from.

sampleQuestions.question: An app needs a predictable structured response. What should the developer do?
options: Ask for JSON-like text and trust it without validating the result
Define the expected structure and validate the response in the app
Parse only the first field and assume the rest are valid
Store the response as executable code and run it as returned
sampleQuestions.explanation: Specify the expected shape and validate the response before using its fields.
whyWrong: Text that resembles JSON can still be malformed or miss required fields.
Partial parsing can hide missing or invalid fields used later.
Generated output should not be executed as trusted application code.

sampleQuestions.question: A user message says “ignore prior rules” inside a document being summarized. How should the app treat it?
options: Allow the document text to replace system and developer instructions
Treat the text as proof that the user has elevated permissions
Disable validation because the document contains an instruction
Treat it as untrusted data and follow the app’s trusted instructions
sampleQuestions.explanation: Treat that text as untrusted content and preserve the application’s trusted instructions.
whyWrong: Untrusted document content must not override the app’s trusted instructions.
A message cannot grant permissions or establish the user’s identity.
The app should keep its normal validation and permission checks.

sampleQuestions.question: A prompt change helps one example but hurts several others. What should the team do?
options: Ship based only on the example that improved
Delete the failing examples so the new prompt looks more successful
Evaluate a representative test set and compare changes before release
Stop monitoring because prompt behavior cannot change after launch
sampleQuestions.explanation: Compare the change on a representative evaluation set before release.
whyWrong: One example cannot show the effect across the workflow’s broader input range.
Removing failures hides regressions instead of measuring them.
Prompts, models, and inputs can change, so ongoing monitoring remains useful.
